title: Kernel Hintscape: lightweight online autotuner for per-request kernel selection
creator: Avery Chen
description: We need a small-footprint, low-latency online autotuner that picks the best kernel implementation per request using a compact "hintscape" feature set (arch fingerprints, seq-len bucket, token-phase, recent latency/cost history). Unlike heavy-weight bandit systems that require large exploration windows, Hintscape should rapidly converge with conservative exploration and safe fallback rules to avoid SLA regressions. The scope covers: 1) feature extraction at request admission (GPU architecture id, SM count, model shard size, seq-len, prefill vs decode, kv-cache hit hints), 2) lightweight scoring model + concurrency-aware safety margins, 3) short-rollout canary and rollback logic, 4) instrumentation and dashboards for per-kernel latency/cost distributions and tail percentiles, and 5) integration points with existing routing and fallback policies. The design must prioritize determinism for canary rollouts and easy opt-out for enterprise Dedicated/Private customers.
acceptance_criteria: Per-request selector implemented in runtime path that returns a kernel token (string) in <= 50us extra overhead for median paths
Selector uses features: architecture fingerprint, seq-len bucket, request phase (prefill/decode), model quantization profile, and recent per-kernel latency estimates
Exploration policy with configurable epsilon and decay that limits additional tail latency risk (configurable threshold)
Safe fallback rules: for any kernel selection that exceeds SLA tail or error rate, route to a verified conservative kernel variant automatically
End-to-end performance tests showing >=6% average token-cost reduction or >=5% median latency improvement across mixed seq-len workloads compared to static kernel policy
Observability: dashboard with per-kernel p50/p95/p99 latencies, token-cost estimates, selection frequency, and rollback triggers
Feature flagging to enable/disable Hintscape at tenant, region, and runtime-level for staged rollouts
comments: 2026-02-12 - Avery Chen: Initial scoping doc uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Kernel+Hintscape+Design. Key design choices outlined: deterministic seeding, per-tenant opt-out, and conservative exploration policy.

2026-02-18 - Samira Patel: PoC of lightweight scorer implemented (Go) in a sidecar harness. Microbenchmarks: selector adds ~42us median overhead on a bare path; still need to optimize to <50us with inlined C paths.

2026-02-24 - Performance team (comment): Ran synthetic mixed-prefill workload (50% prefill 50% decode) on g5x2-like profile. Observed token-cost delta -7.2% with modest increase in p99 latency (+3%). Added constraint to minimize p99 impact via margin tuning.

2026-03-01 - Security review request filed: https://security.redwood.ai/requests/SEC-9876. No blocking crypto/KMS issues but requested explicit audit logging of selection decisions for Private customers.

2026-03-04 - Design review notes from meeting: Use fixed-length seq-len bucketing (1-32,33-128,129-512,>512). Agree to store last-1000 per-kernel latencies in an LRU ring per-executor to compute exponential moving average for quick estimates.
2026-03-07 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4241 (selector + tests). CI failing on one flaky integration test for Canary rollback; investigating.

2026-03-09 - Samira Patel: Integration test fix pushed, tuning of epsilon decay schedule to be more conservative under high load. Added a feature flag: runtime.selector.hintscape.enabled (default false).
2026-03-10 - PM feedback (Jordan Morales): Add end-to-end customer scenario and SLA guardrail config in PRD. Suggested one-month canary on non-critical tenants before org-wide rollout.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: heavier ML-based bandit vs. Hintscape heuristic; chose deterministic lightweight heuristic to reduce complexity and make rollbacks trivial.
Risk: incorrect seq-len bucketing could bias selection toward kernels that perform poorly on edge cases. Mitigation: telemetry-driven re-bucketing and automated canary metrics.
Rollout plan: dev cluster -> internal canary (10% requests) -> staging (selected tenants) -> 60-day org canary -> GA. Feature flag and per-tenant opt-out at each step.
Benchmarks: include mixed chat (short + long) and streaming generation workloads. Baseline against static 'conservative' kernel profile currently used in Dedicated.
